ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effects of KL Regularization in Proximal Policy Optimization for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with using KL regularization in Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for fine-tuning diffusion models. We will compare the performance of PPO with KL regularization to PPO without KL regularization on the text-to-image generation task, using the DDPM model and the LSUN dataset. We will measure the performance using the Inception Score (IS) and the Frechet Inception Distance (FID) metrics.
CONTROLS: We will use PPO without KL regularization as a baseline. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of the KL regularization coefficient and the number of denoising steps on the performance.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance with KL regularization, but the gain may be small. The approach may fail for extremely large-scale settings or for tasks that require more complex KL regularization schemes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of KL-Regularized PPO to Initial Value Function Bias
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the robustness of KL-regularized PPO to the initial value function bias problem in diffusion models. We will modify the KL-regularized PPO to use a learned reverse process that is adaptively adjusted based on the KL divergence between the current and pre-trained distributions. We will evaluate the performance of this approach on the document layout generation task using the Synth10k dataset and compare it to the original KL-regularized PPO.
CONTROLS: We will use the original KL-regularized PPO and the PPO without KL regularization as baselines. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of the adaptive adjustment of the reverse process on the performance.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved robustness to the initial value function bias, but the performance may come at the cost of increased complexity of the approach and potentially higher computational requirements. The approach may fail if the adaptive adjustment of the reverse process is too aggressive or if the KL divergence is not accurately measuring the difference between the distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparison of KL-Regularized PPO and Rejection Sampling for Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We will compare the performance of KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling for fine-tuning diffusion models on the molecule generation task using the ZINC dataset. We will measure the performance using metrics such as the AUPRC (Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve) and the Molecule Ranking Score (MRS).
CONTROLS: We will use rejection sampling with a fixed threshold and a learned threshold as baselines for rejection sampling, and we will also use PPO without KL regularization as a baseline for KL-regularized PPO.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see that rejection sampling performs similarly to KL-regularized PPO in terms of performance, but with lower computational requirements. However, the approach may fail if the fixed or learned threshold is not well chosen, leading to a high rejection rate and inefficient sampling.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigation of the Relationship Between Best-of-N Sampling and KL-Regularized PPO
PROPOSAL: REVISED from Investigating the Effects of KL Regularization in Proximal Policy Optimization for Diffusion Models: We will delve deeper into the theoretical relationship between Best-of-N sampling and KL-regularized PPO for fine-tuning diffusion models. We will derive a theoretical bound on the performance of KL-regularized PPO in terms of the number of denoising steps and the Best-of-N sampling size. We will also provide empirical evidence to validate our theoretical results on the text-to-image generation task using the DDPM model and the LSUN dataset.
CONTROLS: We will use a simplified version of the KL-regularized PPO as a baseline. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of the number of denoising steps and the Best-of-N sampling size on the performance.
COST: 80 GPU-hours (no additional compute needed for the theoretical analysis)
PREDICTION: We expect to see strong theoretical support for the relationship between Best-of-N sampling and KL-regularized PPO. However, the theoretical bound may not reflect the practical performance of the approaches, and additional empirical validation may be needed to fully understand the relationship.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED to Investigative Framework for_hierarchical KL-Regularization in PPO for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL_NUMBER: 1
PROPOSAL: REVISED from Investigating the Effects of KL Regularization in Proximal Policy Optimization for Diffusion Models: We will extend the investigation to a hierarchical KL-regularization framework, where KL-regularization is applied at multiple levels, both at the level of individual denoising steps and at the level of entire denoising trajectories. We will derive a theoretical framework for this hierarchical approach and evaluate its performance on the text-to-image generation task using the DDPM model and the LSUN dataset. We will compare the results to the performance of standard KL-regularized PPO and investigate the effect of the hierarchical regularization on the performance.
CONTROLS: We will use standard KL-regularized PPO, PPO without KL regularization, and a baseline without any KL regularization as controls. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of the number of hierarchical levels and the regularization weights on the performance.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance with the hierarchical KL-regularization framework, but the gain may be small, and the additional complexity of the framework may lead to overfitting issues. The approach may fail if the hierarchical levels are not well-chosen or if the regularization weights are not accurately set.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Auditing the Errors of Pre-trained Flow Models
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the errors of pre-trained flow models using only samples from the data distribution and no explicit reward. We will propose a new approach to correct the errors in the pre-trained flow models by adaptively adjusting the learnable parameters to minimize the distance between the model's output and the data distribution. We will evaluate the performance of our approach on the molecule generation task using the ZINC dataset and compare it to the performance of the original pre-trained flow model and a baseline corrected using an explicit reward.
CONTROLS: We will use the pre-trained flow model and the baseline corrected using an explicit reward as controls. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of the number of iterations and the step size of the adaptive adjustment on the performance.
COST: 160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance with the proposed approach, but the gain may be small, and the additional complexity of the approach may lead to overfitting issues. The approach may fail if the adaptively adjusted learnable parameters are not well-chosen or if the distance between the model's output and the data distribution is not accurately measured.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Impact of Sampling Frequency on Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of sampling frequency on the fine-tuning of diffusion models using KL regularization and rejection sampling. We will analyze the trade-off between sampling frequency and performance, as well as the effect of sampling frequency on the stability and convergence of the training process. We will evaluate the performance of KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling on the text-to-image generation task using the DDPM model and the LSUN dataset with different sampling frequencies.
CONTROLS: We will use standard KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling as controls, as well as a baseline without any sampling frequency adjustment. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of the sampling frequency on the performance.
COST: 140 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see an optimal sampling frequency that balances performance and stability, but the optimal frequency may be difficult to determine and may depend on the specific task and model architecture. The approach may fail if the sampling frequency is not well-chosen or if the training process is not stable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Denoising Schedule on Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of denoising schedule on the fine-tuning of diffusion models using KL regularization and rejection sampling. We will analyze the trade-off between different denoising schedules and performance, as well as the effect of denoising schedule on the stability and convergence of the training process. We will evaluate the performance of KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling on the document layout generation task using the Synth10k dataset with different denoising schedules.
CONTROLS: We will use standard KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling as controls, as well as a baseline without any denoising schedule adjustment. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of the denoising schedule on the performance.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see an optimal denoising schedule that balances performance and stability, but the optimal schedule may be difficult to determine and may depend on the specific task and model architecture. The approach may fail if the denoising schedule is not well-chosen or if the training process is not stable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Generative Quality of Diffusion Models through Implicit Regularization
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the generative quality of diffusion models fine-tuned using KL regularization and rejection sampling by evaluating the implicit regularization effect of the algorithms. We will analyze the trade-off between implicit regularization and explicit regularization, as well as the effect of implicit regularization on the stability and convergence of the training process. We will evaluate the performance of KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling on the molecule generation task using the ZINC dataset and compare it to the performance of a baseline without any regularization.
CONTROLS: We will use standard KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling as controls, as well as a baseline without any regularization. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of implicit regularization on the performance.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see that implicit regularization improves the generative quality of diffusion models, but the gain may be small, and the additional complexity of the approach may lead to overfitting issues. The approach may fail if the implicit regularization is not well-chosen or if the training process is not stable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Batch Normalization on Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the effect of batch normalization on the fine-tuning of diffusion models using KL regularization and rejection sampling. We will analyze the trade-off between batch normalization and performance, as well as the effect of batch normalization on the stability and convergence of the training process. We will evaluate the performance of KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling on the text-to-image generation task using the DDPM model and the LSUN dataset with and without batch normalization.
CONTROLS: We will use standard KL-regularized PPO and rejection sampling as controls, as well as a baseline without any batch normalization adjustment. We will also conduct ablations to investigate the effect of batch normalization on the performance.
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see that batch normalization improves the stability and convergence of the training process, but the gain may be small, and the additional complexity of the approach may lead to overfitting issues. The approach may fail if the batch normalization is not well-chosen or if the training process is not stable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Principled KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of replacing the trajectory KL constraint with a samples-per-mode (SPM) regularization, which is computationally tractable and controls the mode coverage of the fine-tuned diffusion model.
CONTROLS: Compare against training without KL regularization (unregularized baseline) and a relaxation of the trajectory KL divergence (empirical KL baseline).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that the SPM regularization will outperform both the unregularized and empirical KL baselines in terms of mode coverage and fine-tuned model quality, with potential trade-offs in convergence speed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sampling-Based Fine-Tuning with Mode Coverage Control
PROPOSAL: Devise a novel rejection sampling scheme that selects high-reward samples based on their mode coverage, leveraging the computationally tractable SPM regularization from Proposal 1.
CONTROLS: Compare against a standard rejection sampling baseline without mode coverage control, and ablate the effect of different reward functions and SPM regularization strengths.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (leveraging samples already generated in Proposal 1).
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed rejection sampling scheme will achieve higher reward and better model quality than the standard baseline, with a greater improvement when coupled with the SPM regularization, and potentially biased mode coverage.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Principled KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Explore an augmented KL-regularization term that penalizes the KL divergence between the fine-tuned distribution and the original distribution of the pre-trained diffusion model's noise schedule (augmented KL term), aiming to mitigate the initial value function bias problem.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original KL-regularization term and analyze the effect of different hyperparameters (augmentation strength, KL weight).
COST: 50 GPU-hours (modifications to existing code).
PREDICTION: We expect that introducing the augmented KL term will improve the fine-tuned model's stability and quality, with potential convergence benefits in large-scale settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flow Model Adaptation via Cycle Consistency
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel adaptation method for flow models that leverages cycle consistency between the pre-trained and fine-tuned models to correct errors without explicit reward signals.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of fine-tuning with KL regularization (from Proposal 1) and evaluate the adaptation quality using metrics such as Frechet Inception Distance (FID) score.
COST: 150 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed adaptation method will effectively reduce the discrepancy between the fine-tuned flow model and the target data distribution, with potential improvements in sample quality and diversity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate a hierarchical fine-tuning approach that adapts the pre-trained diffusion model in a hierarchical manner, starting with coarsely-structured representations and progressively refining the outputs towards more detailed and accurate features.
CONTROLS: Compare against a standard fine-tuning baseline and evaluate the impact of hierarchical fine-tuning on model quality using metrics such as FID and Inception Score (IS).
COST: 250 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect that the hierarchical fine-tuning approach will improve the fine-tuned model's ability to capture complex and nuanced features in the target data distribution, with potential trade-offs in training complexity and computational cost.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Hierarchical Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Modify the hierarchical fine-tuning approach to incorporate the SPM regularization from Proposal 1, which encourages the fine-tuned diffusion model to have better mode coverage.
CONTROLS: Compare against the baseline hierarchical fine-tuning without SPM regularization and evaluate the impact of adding SPM regularization on model quality using metrics such as FID and IS.
COST: 25 GPU-hours (integration of SPM regularization into existing code).
PREDICTION: We expect that adding SPM regularization will improve the performance of hierarchical fine-tuning in terms of mode coverage and overall model quality, while potentially introducing minor trade-offs in convergence speed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning with Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of multi-task learning to fine-tune diffusion models on multiple related tasks simultaneously, leveraging the shared representations learned during pre-training to adapt to new tasks more efficiently.
CONTROLS: Compare against single-task fine-tuning baselines and evaluate the impact of multi-task fine-tuning on model quality using metrics such as FID and IS, as well as task-specific evaluation metrics.
COST: 300 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect that multi-task fine-tuning will lead to improved adaptability and efficiency in fine-tuning diffusion models, with potential trade-offs in training complexity and model specialization to individual tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Text-to-Image Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models for Domain Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of diffusion models for text-to-image domain adaptation, fine-tuning a pre-trained model on a new domain using a limited number of samples from that domain, and evaluating the performance of the fine-tuned model on downstream tasks such as image captioning and object detection.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art text-to-image synthesis models and evaluate the impact of fine-tuning on model quality using metrics such as FID and IS, as well as downstream task evaluation metrics.
COST: 350 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect that fine-tuning a diffusion model on a new domain will lead to improved performance on image captioning and object detection tasks, with potential trade-offs in fine-tuning efficiency and model overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Denoising Schedules for Efficient Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of adaptive denoising schedules that adjust the level of noise reduction during fine-tuning based on the progress of the optimization process, aiming to improve fine-tuning efficiency and effectiveness.
CONTROLS: Compare against fixed denoising schedules and evaluate the impact of adaptive denoising on model quality using metrics such as FID and IS, as well as computational cost and convergence speed.
COST: 200 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: We expect that adaptive denoising schedules will lead to improved fine-tuning efficiency and effectiveness, with potential trade-offs in convergence speed and model quality.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Evaluation and Empirical Guidelines for Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed fine-tuning methods across various diffusion models, tasks, and datasets, and provide empirical guidelines for practitioners on when to use each method, taking into account factors such as model quality, computational cost, and convergence speed.
CONTROLS: Comparison of proposed methods across various scenarios and evaluation metrics.
COST: 400 GPU-hours (leveraging results from previous experiments).
PREDICTION: We expect that the comprehensive evaluation and empirical guidelines will provide valuable insights and practical recommendations for practitioners working with diffusion models, helping to reduce the complexity and increase the effectiveness of fine-tuning these models.

TITLE: Investigating the Effects of Activation Normalization on Steering Primitives
PROPOSAL: We conduct an ablation study on the behavior of activation addition and directional ablation across LLMs that apply RMS normalization before every attention and MLP block. Specifically, we will compare their performance on a range of benchmarks, including a designed suite of experiments showcasing how normalization affects feature interactions, with/without normalized and unnormalized activation inputs.
CONTROLS: Compare against an identical model architecture that does not apply RMS normalization.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to observe a more pronounced limitation of the current steering primitives in normalized activations, with a deterioration of control over unwanted behaviors as the effect of model outputs builds and becomes more pronounced despite normalization between later processing blocks. However, the robustness of this assertion to a range of activation normalization strengths needs to be tested.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Robustness of Coordinate-Specific Steering Approach Across Models and Training Regimes
PROPOSAL: We conduct a comprehensive study to evaluate the robustness of our enhanced coordinate-specific steering approach across various LLM models (e.g., language models of different sizes and complexities), training regimes (e.g., pre-training objectives, warm-up strategies, and dataset sizes), and hyperparameter settings. We will also explore its performance under different normalizing flows and projection techniques.
CONTROLS: Conduct experiments across a range of models (e.g., BERT, RoBERTa, Longformer), training objectives (e.g., masked language modeling, next sentence prediction), and hyperparameters (e.g., learning rate, batch size, weight decay). Compare our approach against existing steering methods under different normalizing flows and projection techniques.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our method to maintain its performance across various LLM models, training regimes, and hyperparameter settings, while showing improved robustness compared to existing steering methods. However, we may observe some degradation in performance when using very large models or heavily normalized activations, suggesting that our method may require further adaptation for extreme settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Guided Activation Steering with Gradient-based Anchor Points
PROPOSAL: We propose a guided activation steering approach, which utilizes gradient-based anchor points to identify critical feature directions and their corresponding activation values. Our method adaptively learns to amplify or suppress these critical features, enabling more precise control over model behavior. We experiment with different anchor point selection strategies, such as gradient-based and soft-margin-based methods, to evaluate their effectiveness.
CONTROLS: Compare our guided activation steering approach against the enhanced coordinate-specific steering approach from Proposal 3, and evaluate its performance on a range of benchmarks for refusal of harmful requests, emotion control of generated text, and overall model performance.
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our guided activation steering approach to provide more precise control over model behavior, with improved performance on benchmarks for refusal of harmful requests and emotion control of generated text. However, we may observe increased computational costs due to the additional anchor point selection process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Interplay between Activation Steering and Model Exponents
PROPOSAL: We investigate the relationship between activation steering and model exponents, exploring how steering operations affect the stiffness or softness of the model's behavior. We propose a theoretical framework to analyze the interplay between steering and exponents, and use it to derive insights into the optimal steering strategies for different objectives (e.g., refusal of harmful requests, emotion control).
CONTROLS: Develop mathematical models to simulate the behavior of LLMs under different steering strategies, and compare the results against empirical evaluations on real-world benchmarks.
COST: 600 GPU-hours (primarily for theoretical analysis and simulations)
PREDICTION: We expect our framework to provide a deeper understanding of the interplay between activation steering and model exponents, and to identify optimal steering strategies for different objectives. However, we may need to address potential limitations of the theoretical framework, such as its reliance on simplifying assumptions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-world Evaluation of Activation Steering for Emotional Control
PROPOSAL: We conduct a real-world evaluation of our activation steering approaches to assess their effectiveness on emotion control tasks. We collect a dataset of text generated by LLMs on a range of emotional topics and perform a critical comparison of our approaches with existing baselines.
CONTROLS: Compare our activation steering approaches (coordinate-specific steering, guided activation steering) with existing emotion control baselines, such as factorized emotion control and emotion aware models. Evaluate our approaches using metrics such as perplexity, emotion recognition accuracy, and human evaluation scores.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our activation steering approaches to outperform existing baselines on emotion control tasks, particularly in terms of achieving more nuanced and contextualized emotional responses. However, we may observe some trade-offs between the expressiveness of the LLM's emotional responses and the coherence of the generated text.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large-Scale Comparison of Activation Steering Methods for Refusal of Harmful Requests
PROPOSAL: We conduct a large-scale comparison of our activation steering approaches (coordinate-specific steering, guided activation steering) with existing baselines to assess their effectiveness on refusal of harmful requests. We collect a dataset of text generated by LLMs on a range of harmful topics and evaluate our approaches using metrics such as recall, precision, and F1-score.
CONTROLS: Compare our activation steering approaches with existing baselines, such as rules-based systems and adjective-noun pairing methods. Evaluate our approaches using metrics such as recall, precision, and F1-score.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our activation steering approaches to outperform existing baselines on refusal of harmful requests, particularly in terms of achieving high recall and precision while maintaining good F1-score. However, we may observe some trade-offs between the strictness of the refusal and the coherence of the generated text.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Towards a Unified Framework for Activation Steering: Multi-Task Learning and Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a unified framework for activation steering that enables multi-task learning and transfer learning across different objectives, such as refusal of harmful requests, emotional control, and language understanding. Our framework incorporates a shared representation of activation steering and task-specific ranking mechanisms to enable flexible and efficient adaptation.
CONTROLS: Compare our unified framework with existing activation steering approaches and baselines using metrics such as task-specific performance, adaptation speed, and model generalization.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our unified framework to achieve state-of-the-art performance on a range of tasks while maintaining efficient adaptation and generalization. However, we may need to address potential trade-offs between the shared representation and task-specific ranking mechanisms.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Augmenting Activation Steering with Scale-Aware Editorial Primitives
PROPOSAL: 
To rectify the shortcomings of existing activation steering approaches, we propose combining directional ablation and activation addition with a novel vector scaling control, which adjusts the magnitude of the feature vector before applying directional ablation or activation addition. This control enables more precise granular control over the target behavior, by scaling down the effect of an ablation or addition and allowing for partial suppression, removal, or inversion of the behavior.

CONTROLS: 
- compare to directional ablation and activation addition alone
- evaluate ablation studies eliminating the vector scaling component
- examine how well scaling controls align with user instruction, across various test cases with real user data

COST: 
100,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: 
Based on our theoretical considerations, we predict that models with more opacity in activation norms across deeper layers will benefit most from vector scaling. We anticipate it may outperform traditional ablation in scenarios with strong discontinuity, such as asking a model to completely refrain from inferring emotional content when discussing sensitive topics. However, poorly chosen scaling parameters could degrade model performance, indicating additional research into principled scaling methods.

Relevant experimental domain: LLM safety: refusal of harmful requests (jailbreaking)

TITLE: Orthogonalization Framework for Activation Steering Operations
PROPOSAL: 
To elucidate the relative effects of orthogonalization in activation steering, we propose a systematic framework for analyzing orthogonalization mechanisms like directional ablation and their relation to activation norms. This framework involves deriving the propagation of orthogonalization edits through multilayer nested RMS normalized activation spaces and analyzing how interaction between orthogonal components contributes to the overall efficacy of the edit. TITLE: Dual-Path Architecture for Adaptive Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a dual-path architecture that combines the benefits of both activation steering and dual-training. The first path consists of a pre-trained language model with a fixed set of steering operations (e.g., activation addition and ablation). The second path consists of a separate model trained using a dual-training objective that encourages the model to correct any undesirable behaviors induced by the steering operations. The two paths are connected to form a loop, where the output of the steering operations is used as input to the dual-training model, which in turn modifies the input to the steering operations. This architecture allows for adaptive and flexible control over model behavior.

- controlling for model overfitting and evaluating transferability of steering operations

TITLE: "Spatial and Focal Dimensional Convolutions for Depth-from-Focus"
PROPOSAL: We propose a new neural network architecture that incorporates spatial and focal dimensional convolutions to leverage the unique structure of focal stacks. This architecture consists of a backbone network that performs feature extraction from all-in-focus images, a spatial dimension convolutional module that aggregates information across neighboring pixels, and a focal dimension convolutional module that captures the focus evolution across the focal stack. The output of these two modules is then combined through a cross-modal attention mechanism to produce the final depth map. We will train this architecture using a combination of recent DFF benchmarks, and evaluate its performance on both quantitative metrics (e.g., mean absolute error, root mean squared error) and qualitative metrics (e.g., visual assessment of depth maps).
CONTROLS: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) trained using traditional bottom-up focus estimation followed by up-sample filtering to infer depth, CNNs trained end-to-end on focal stacks without any spatial or focal attention.
COST: Estimated: 300 GPU-hours (large-scale focal stack datasets, variant network architectures)
PREDICTION: Our architecture will achieve competitive state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on standard DFF benchmarks, with noticeable gains over baseline CNN methods on fine-textured or reflective regions and at abrupt depth changes. Due to its weak generalizability to novel textures or depth variations, our proposed model might fail when trained on a narrow training set (e.g., specific types of textures or depth changes).

TITLE: "Physics-Guided Depth-from-Focus Network"
PROPOSAL: To incorporate physical knowledge into our learning-based DFF model, we introduce a physics-guided module that mimics the focus behavior of light in a camera. This module uses a combination of Gaussian filters and anisotropic diffusion to simulate the blurring effect of out-of-focus light, and the resulting "ideal blurred images" are then used as a regularization term in the loss function. We hypothesize that training on this term will encourage our model to capture the underlying physics of DFF and improve its robustness to texture-induced artifacts. To evaluate the effectiveness of this module, we will train our model on the NYU Depth Map Dataset with and without the physics-guided module.

PREDICTION: Our physics-guided network will exhibit improved robustness over the spatial and focal dimensional convolutions model (1) on texture-induced artifacts and abrupt depth changes, given a moderate increase in training time and model complexity. TITLE: Temporal Offset-Denoising Exploration (TODE)
PROPOSAL: Develop TODE, an efficient offline exploration strategy aimed at learning about the episode-wise observation offsets without any explicit state estimation or additional online interaction. This offset predictor inputs the past cumulative loss (or say, optimism) values and produces a single, 'locally consistent' offset offset estimate per exploration path in each episode. PROPOSAL: Introduce a probabilistic approach for predicting the evolving observation offsets, DROF, which uses a conditional normalizing flow-based model to generate an approximate distribution over possible offset sequences. The key idea is to model the offset dynamics as a Markov process, where the probability of an offset given a sequence of past offsets is represented by a neural network. DROF learn to predict the transition probabilities of this Markov process and the initial offset distribution, allowing for robust offset forecasting and robustness to offset uncertainties.

PROPOSAL: We design an experiment to investigate the impact of token-level interleaving on the computational efficiency and training stability of multi-modal chain-of-thought reasoning. Specifically, we interleave visual and textual tokens at the token level, using a variant of the CoT architecture with a separate visual encoder and decoder, and a shared textual encoder-decoder. TITLE: Adaptive Visual Tokenization for Long-Range Dependency Modeling
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the quadratic growth of sequence lengths due to interleaved visual and textual tokens, we propose an experiment to investigate the use of adaptive visual tokenization. We adaptively sample visual tokens based on the expected computationally expensive operations in the reasoning chain, such as visual state transitions or compositional reasoning steps. We use a learnable tokenization module that takes into account the context and task-specific requirements, and dynamically adjusts the level of tokenization.
CONTROLS: We compare our adaptive tokenization approach to a fixed tokenization approach, as well as a baseline with no tokenization.
COST: Estimated 8,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved computational efficiency and training stability, with a moderate trade-off in performance due to the reduced visual token space. Performance may improve on tasks that require compositional reasoning.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Multi-Turn Agentic Search with Intrinsic Step Rewards (MAIR)
REVISED PROPOSAL: Build on the idea of proposal 1 and develop an intrinsic process reward mechanism called Multi-Turn Agentic Reward (MATR) that is specifically designed for agentic search tasks, especially open-domain question-answering and multi-hop question-answering settings. MATR combines the strengths of risk-sensitive temporal difference learning and efficient exploration-exploitation trade-off, thus further incentivizes evaluating intermediate states. MATR will be designed to encourage the agent to focus on turn-by-turn progress and improved decision-making along the search process. We will explore different variants of MATR that adapt to the specific task and environment.
CONTROLS:
  1. GRPO baseline (norm outcome rewards within each group).
  2. Random Intrinsic Rewards (RIR) variant of MAIR (for baseline comparison).
  3. Baseline without any intrinsic rewards.
COST: 1000 (approximately 10% overhead compared to baseline GRPO)
PREDICTION: MAIR may reduce the problem of advantage collapse by 0.3 average-AUC (see figures 4-5), achieve better sample efficiency than baseline GRPO (Figure 6), and provide more accurate search outcomes than baseline GRPO (Table 7). MAIR may fail to improve performance in highly symmetric tasks where exploration is not necessary.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: MAIR-RIC: Adapting MATR Reward with State-Reward Aggregation
PROPOSAL: Introduce a state-reward aggregation method that complements the intrinsic step rewards of proposal 1. The method, called Reward-Independent Context (RIC), will aggregate intermediate rewards based on the current state of the search environment. We will explore two RIC variations: one based on the similarity between the current state and the goal state (RIC-Sim), and another based on the novelty of the current state in the context of the entire search history (RIC-Novel).
CONTROLS:
  1. MAIR-RIC-Sim (using similarity-based aggregation).
  2. MAIR-RIC-Novel (using novelty-based aggregation).
  3. MAIR without RIC (baseline).
COST: 1200 (approximately 15% overhead compared to baseline GRPO)
PREDICTION: MAIR-RIC may further reduce the problem of advantage collapse by 0.2 average-AUC, achieve even better sample efficiency than MAIR (Figure 7), and provide more accurate search outcomes than MAIR (Table 8). MAIR-RIC may introduce bias in tasks with highly variable state spaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamic Exploration Bonus for Agentic Search
PROPOSAL: Introduce a dynamic exploration bonus to the intrinsic step rewards, which encourages the agent to explore new and unseen states in the search environment. The bonus will be calculated based on the novelty of the current state and will be adjusted dynamically based on the agent's progress and the difficulty of the task. We will explore two variants of the bonus: one that is based on the KL divergence between the current state and the agent's past experiences (KL-Bonus), and another that is based on the density of the current state in the context of the entire search space (Density-Bonus).
CONTROLS:
  1. GRPO baseline (norm outcome rewards within each group).
  2. MAIR-RIC with KL-Bonus (for baseline comparison).
  3. MAIR-RIC with Density-Bonus (for baseline comparison).
COST: 800 (approximately 10% overhead compared to baseline GRPO)
PREDICTION: The exploration bonus may lead to faster knowledge acquisition in early stages of search, improved performance in tasks with complex search spaces (Table 9), and faster convergence of the agent's policy (Figure 8). However, it may also lead to over-exploration in tasks with simple search spaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Reward Masking for Multi-Turn Agentic Search
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hierarchical reward masking mechanism that selectively masks the intrinsic step rewards for different stages of the search process. The mechanism will be based on the search task's abstract representation and will take into account the agent's progress and the relevance of the current state to the final goal. We will explore two variants of the mechanism: one that uses a binary mask (Binary-Mask), and another that uses a continuous mask (Continuous-Mask).
CONTROLS:
  1. GRPO baseline (norm outcome rewards within each group).
  2. MAIR-RIC with Binary-Mask (for baseline comparison).
  3. MAIR-RIC with Continuous-Mask (for baseline comparison).
COST: 900 (approximately 12% overhead compared to baseline GRPO)
PREDICTION: The hierarchical reward masking may lead to more stable training of the agent's policy, improved performance in tasks with multiple search stages (Table 10), and reduced variance of the agent's behavior (Figure 9). However, it may also lead to under-training of the agent in tasks with simple search stages.

TITLE: Fully Supervised Learning for One-Step Image AR Models
PROPOSAL: Train a one-step generator model directly on a labeled dataset where each sample consists of a sequence of tokens and their corresponding ground-truth probability vectors. The generator takes a latent variable drawn from a prior distribution as input and outputs the entire token sequence, without relying on a predefined noise-to-data mapping. TITLE: Trajectory KL Regularization via Self-Supervised Best-of-N Sampling
PROPOSAL: We develop a novel regularization method for KL-regularized fine-tuning by employing Best-of-N sampling: for each batch of samples generated by the fine-tuned model, we select the top-N samples with the greatest reward. These selected samples form a subset of the generated samples, and we optimize the fine-tuned model to reproduce this subset while maintaining a fixed KL divergence between the entire set of generated samples and the subset. The resulting loss functions leverages the gradient of the marginal likelihood of the subset, which is analogous to the policy gradient objective in reinforcement learning. We test this approach with the pre-trained DALL-E 2 model on text-to-image generation and compare with the performance of the PPO model described in our first experiment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tri-Component Contrastive Learning for External Context Utilization
PROPOSAL: Develop a tri-component contrastive learning framework that consists of three components: (1) external context augmentation, (2) internal knowledge masking, and (3) response generation. In the external context augmentation component, the external context is augmented with artificial contradicting statements to simulate hallucinations. In the internal knowledge masking component, the internal knowledge of the model is masked to prevent over-reliance on it. In the response generation component, the model generates responses given the augmented external context and the masked internal knowledge. The framework will be trained in a contrastive fashion, where the model is encouraged to generate responses that are close to the ground truth but far from the artificial hallucinations. The resulting framework will be evaluated on a set of real-world benchmark datasets for hallucination detection in RAG systems.
CONTROLS: Compare to the unsupervised masked language model-based external context utility scoring model (proposal 1), the GNN-based dependency graph model (proposal 2), and the pronoun-based scoring model (proposal 3).
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: The tri-component contrastive learning framework shows significant improvement over the baseline methods, especially in capturing the relationship between external context and internal knowledge usage, which leads to better performance in hallucination detection.

TITLE: A Simple Turn-Level Reward Mechanism
PROPOSAL: We propose a turn-level reward mechanism, termed "Intrinsic Step Evaluation" (ISE), which computes a propensity score for each interaction turn by modeling the explainable discrepancies between corresponding rollout trajectories in a given group. ISE utilizes a two-stage approach: first, text-based alignments via the masked language model (e.g., BERT) are used to measure representational disagreement between turns of high-performing and poorly performing trajectories; second, gradient-based feature importance assessment leverages the policy model's PoLinator (a learned classifier) to quantify how each feature (word or subtoken) contributes to the success and failure metrics from the initial turn to each subsequent step. This process yields a compact turn-level reward signal reflecting both representational and decisional novelty.
CONTROLS: We will benchmark ISE against variants involving stronger aligners (e.g., attention-based, equivariant), incentive mechanisms (e.g., exponential, linear), and factor representation maps (no baseline).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probing the Necessity of Independence of Representation Space and Solution Space
PROPOSAL: We will adapt a recent generative adversarial network (GAN) model, StyleGAN2, to generate synthetic solutions to ETSP, effectively decoupling the generation of solution and representation spaces. This model will be trained to generate solutions for a fixed ETSP instance size, where the representation space is comprised of variations in the neural network architecture (student model), and the solution space is comprised of permutations of the nodes (trajectories). We will study the impact of increasing the size of the solution space (by increasing the number of nodes) on the performance of a fixed-size student model, while measuring the increase in complexity of the corresponding GAN model. We will quantify the relationship between the student model performance and the complexity of the GAN model.
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline study where the GAN model generates proposals and solutions simultaneously, tightly coupling the two spaces.
COST: 9720 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find a power-law relationship between the complexity of the GAN model and the student model's performance as the solution space grows, and that the fragile limits of deep learning models are closely tied to the representation complexity of the problem, which cannot be decoupled in most existing models.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Revised: Probing the Necessity of Independence of Representation Space and Solution Space
PROPOSAL: We will modify the GAN-based setup to use a variational autoencoder (VAE) to generate solutions to ETSP, effectively decoupling the generation of solution and representation spaces. This will be done by having the VAE model learn to represent solutions to ETSP as a distribution over permutation-invariant embeddings, and then using a student model to predict these embeddings directly. We will study the impact of increasing the size of the solution space (by increasing the number of nodes) on the performance of a fixed-size student model, while measuring the increase in complexity of the corresponding VAE model. We will quantify the relationship between the student model performance and the complexity of the VAE model.
CONTROLS: Compare to the baseline study from Proposal 2 and a new baseline where the VAE model generates proposals and solutions simultaneously.
COST: 6290 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to find a similar power-law relationship between the complexity of the VAE model and the student model's performance as the solution space grows, but potentially with less overfitting and a more robust relationship due to the permutation-invariant properties of the VAE.

TITLE: Probing the Necessity of Independence of Representation Space and Solution Space
PROPOSAL: We will further modify the setup by generating solutions to ETSP using reinforcement learning (RL) with a permutation-invariant embedding as the critic.
